top_signals.title: Multiple Dead After 7.1-Magnitude Quake Hits Japan
top_signals.summary:
Rescuers continued the hunt for survivors in the ruins of a shopping mall on the southwestern island of Kyushu on Wednesday, after a major earthquake in which multiple people have been confirmed dead.

The quake hit a region that is a hub for Japan's semiconductor industry, housing names like TSMC and Tokyo Electron. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: The First Waves of Amphibious Assault Will Be Unmanned
top_signals.summary:
In the Pacific War, the U.S. Navy’s underwater demolition teams prepared the way for U.S. and allied amphibious landings on enemy-held islands. Through beach reconnaissance, obstacle breaching, mine clearance, and other missions, these teams paved paths for the first waves of amphibious assaults conducted by naval task forces and subsequent landings by marines and soldiers throughout the island hopping campaign.  These critical first steps of an amphibious operation were incredibly risky in World War II. And the underwater demolition teams, which were the predecessors of the Navy SEALs, were understandably proud of their work.
